analysis: Examined the three changed files. (1) provider-swift/Package.swift line 166-167 adds the swift-transformers `Hub` product to ProviderCore. It comes from an existing, already-pinned package (from: 1.3.0), so no new package URL or supply-chain source is introduced. The residual risk is the newly linked module surface, which is not security-relevant on its face. (2) docs/reference/configuration.md lines 498-507 document DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE, _MB, _VERIFY, TEMPLATE_LOOPS and COLD_LOAD_RELEASE. The prompt-token cache reuses token IDs of rendered template pieces 'already seen in the request's prefix-cache scope'. It also forwards its settings through the LaunchAgent, and the global DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE disable turns it off. Relevant to T-041 (cross-tenant cache and timing oracle, SEC-035): this is a new in-memory cache whose lookups affect time-to-first-token. Per the docs it is keyed per prefix-cache scope, and that scope is coordinator-authored from account, model and contract identity. If the scope keying is correct, cross-account reuse is not enabled. A same-account timing oracle already falls under accepted risk SEC-035. The implementation (PromptTokenCache.swift) is not supplied, so I could not verify scope isolation or whether the cache persists to disk. The threat model's T-041 does not mention this new in-memory tier and should be updated once the source is reviewed. The cold-load-release setting lets later coordinator events overtake a request waiting for its model load (ProviderLoop+WorkFIFO.swift, not supplied). That could affect ordering and cancellation (T-010), so the next pass should confirm cancel and authorization-generation checks still apply. (3) The added PromptPreparationBenchmark.swift (306 lines) is a benchmark-only tool run via `darkbloom benchmark --prompt-prep`. It uses synthetic conversations and the local tokenizer, with no network, key or coordinator interaction visible. Only metadata and a truncated patch were supplied, with no head text, so its content is not fully reviewed. No concrete regression is identified from the supplied evidence. Integration should examine PromptTokenCache scope keying, memory bounds (up to 4096 MiB per tokenizer) and background verification.
